title: Belly Fat in Women: Why It's Hard to Lose and What Really Works
intro: You can't burn belly fat from just one spot. It goes down when your overall body fat goes down, and it's often one of the last areas to change, so patience and consistency are the key.

sections.h: Why the belly becomes a fat storage spot
sections.p: Where your body stores fat is strongly influenced by genetics, hormones and age. Many women notice their belly gains more easily after age 35, when hormones start to change. Long-term stress and lack of sleep can also play a part.

Doing 100 sit-ups a day will strengthen your stomach muscles, but it won't burn the fat on top of them. Same goes for the many gadgets and gels that are 'special for the belly'. Fat comes off your whole body in an order decided by your own body.

Eat a little less than your body needs, in a moderate way, and make sure you get enough protein. Do strength training 2 to 3 times a week to protect your muscles. Add more daily steps and take care of your sleep. This combination is what helps fat, including belly fat, go down over time.

sections.h: Bloating is not the same as fat
sections.p: A belly that is flat in the morning but bloated in the evening is usually due to bloating, not fat. Certain foods, constipation, eating too fast or the days before your period can cause bloating. Drinking enough water and eating slowly can help.

If your belly suddenly gets bigger, feels painful, your periods are irregular, or you suspect PCOS or a thyroid problem, see a doctor. If there's a chance you're pregnant, get your doctor's advice first. Don't try to fix it yourself with a strict diet.

action: Measure your waist once a week on the same day and at the same time.
Do 20 minutes of strength training 3 times this week: squats, wall push-ups, glute bridges and planks.
Fill half your plate with vegetables at lunch and dinner.
Cut sweet drinks down to once a day or less.
Walk for 10 to 15 minutes after dinner.
myth: Many believe wearing a corset or wrapping your belly in plastic can 'melt' belly fat. Actually, what comes out is only sweat, which is water, and it comes back when you drink. Fat doesn't melt this way.

faq.q: Why has my weight gone down but my belly still looks the same?
faq.a: The belly is often one of the last areas to shrink. Measure your waist and take photos every 2 to 4 weeks, because small changes are really hard to see in the mirror every day.

faq.q: Do I need to do crunches every day?
faq.a: No need to do them every day. Core training is great for strength and posture, but it doesn't specifically burn belly fat. It's better to focus on full-body exercise.

faq.q: Is it really harder after age 35?
faq.a: For many women, yes, it's a bit more challenging because of hormonal changes. The strategy stays the same, but strength training and protein become more important. If you have symptoms that bother you, discuss them with your doctor.
